summary:
Where the minutes go (read from the three logs and the code; nothing was run).

1. Not fleet start-up. Starting a file's stand-in fleet costs about 0.3 s on the quiet run and at most 3 s on the loaded ones: under 1% of any run. Sharing one fleet between files would save almost nothing.

2. Operations on the stand-in fleet. 66 tests of 10 s or more are 88% of quiet test time; four files (workflows, across, validate, change) are 57%. Each of those tests is a handful of starts, stops and restarts, and an operation is mostly fleet scans: one scan starts about 430 processes and takes 4.1 s quiet, 11 s loaded. A start does 4 scans and a stop 2, and roughly 100 of those scans repeat one made a moment earlier.

3. Split. Judged by how each test slows under load (scan-only tests x2.9, fixed-wait tests x1.0), quiet test time is about 54% scanning and 46% fixed waits; loaded it is about 77% / 23%. The fixed waits are: a 5 s sleep before every load check (about 64 loads), two 60 s stalls in across (the stall limit is multiplied by SLOW), 40-62 s timeouts in state and ask, 15-20 s start-of-service timers, and 16 s sleeps.

4. Loaded versus quiet. The same 632 tests take x2.0; on top of that, 27 newer tests in four files add 648 s of test time in gate25.

Cuts. None weakens a test except cut 9, which is marked. The big ones are fewer scans per operation (1), fewer processes per scan (2, 5), a 1 s load poll on the stand-in (3), across's stall limit not multiplied by SLOW (4) and longest files first (6). The scan savings overlap, so the list does not add up; together I project roughly 650 s (give or take 100) for today's suite at 2 at once on a quiet Mac, against about 1210 s now. That is a projection, not a measurement.

What the service-side cuts cost. Cuts 1, 3 and 8 edit functions that are in workflow fingerprints (deploy, stopContainer, clusterDeploy, clusterParts, restartJob, downloadVersion). Start, start-across, stop and restart then get new versions and need their validation run on the real Sparks, so they belong in one build. Every service edit also needs tools/build-server.mjs and tools/code-map.mjs, which build.test checks.

Spark 2 (projection, not measured). Without the security software a scan should cost a fraction, so fixed waits dominate there: SLOW=1, cuts 3, 4 and 7, and longest-first at 8 at once bring the gate down to about its longest file. Two things matter there that don't on the Mac: every command to offline spark1 sleeps 1 s (service/src/02-ssh.mjs:7), which becomes the floor of a scan; and tests that lean on operations being slow will race (see flaky).

Limits of this analysis. I could not time a process start on this Mac (the command was not permitted), so cuts 2 and 5 assume scan time follows process count; time one scan before and after. The logs carry no file names or hook times: tests were mapped to files by name and order, and a two-slot schedule built from that reproduces the three walls within 4-17 s.

Quick check while developing (never the gate): door, cli, passkey, internet, fuzz, api, agent-setup, build and fleet are about 166 s of test time quiet, about a minute and a half at 2 at once.

FIXED WAITS VERSUS SCANNING, per file, quiet, assuming scan work slows x2.9 under load and fixed waits x1.0: all files 942 s fixed (46%) and 1092 s scanning (54%) of 2034 s; loaded about 23% / 77%.

Fixed share by file (quiet): fleet 86%, ask 69%, state 69%, heal 64%, across 55% (181 s), desired 44%, pause 42%, change 41% (106 s), workflows 40% (122 s), validate 40% (110 s), gateway 35%; fuzz, door, cli about 0%.

Whole files that are all scanning: fuzz x3.2, door x3.2, cli x3.0. The long operation tests sit at x2.0-2.4. across 'parts that never connect' is the least sensitive long test (x1.5) because about 138 s of it is two 60 s stalls.
SPARK_TEST_SLOW=3 adds real waiting, not only limits: across's stall limit is 20 s x SLOW (two stalls: about 138 s instead of about 50 s) and ask's hold is 3 x SLOW + 3 s (12 s instead of 6 s).

SCHEDULE. Node sorts files by name. Today's suite at quiet speeds (2330 s of test time): 2 at once 1210 s by name, 1166 s longest-first; 4 at once 737 / 585 s; 8 at once 491 / 329 s (329 s is the across file).

cuts.title: Scan the fleet once per operation step, not two or three times
cuts.what: deploy() scans the fleet in plan() (line 123), again at 130 only to look the model up, and again in stopContainer (185) for each stop; clusterDeploy does the same (08-cluster.mjs:325, 333); a stop scans in its action (17-changes.mjs:529, 24-handler.mjs:464) and again in its job. Pass the first scan along. About 100 scans go: 4.1 s each quiet, 11 s loaded.
cuts.risk: Edits deploy, stopContainer and clusterDeploy, which are in the workflow fingerprints: start, start-across and stop get new versions and each needs its validation run on the real Sparks after the install. A stop would trust a scan a few seconds old to find a two-Spark model's other part. The count of 100 comes from reading the tests, not from a measurement. On a loaded machine the saving is nearer 470 s.

cuts.title: Fewer processes per fleet scan in the scan script
cuts.what: INVENTORY_SCRIPT starts about 14 processes per model folder and 15 per cache entry: basename, cat|base64|tr, du|cut, and ls|head|base64|tr even when there are no GGUF files. Bash built-ins and skipping the empty pipelines roughly halve that, about 430 to 290 processes per scan. On this Mac each process start is what costs; a scan takes 4.1 s quiet.
cuts.risk: Assumes scan time follows the number of processes started; that is inferred from the logs, not measured, so time one scan before and after. This is the production script that runs on the real Sparks over SSH: its output has to stay exactly the same. It is not in any workflow fingerprint. Overlaps with cut 1: together they save less than the two numbers added.

cuts.title: Load poll of 5 s configurable; stand-in models load in 1 s
cuts.what: Every start and restart sleeps 5 s before its first look (also 08-cluster.mjs:426, 17-changes.mjs:592, 13-main-model.mjs:209), and the stand-in answers after 4 s (test/mock/bin/curl:13 and :21, test/mock/model.mjs:28). A poll knob honoured only with ALL_LOCAL (1 s) and a 1 s stand-in load save about 3.5 s on each of about 64 loads.
cuts.risk: Edits the text of deploy, clusterParts and restartJob once, so start, start-across and restart get new versions to validate on the Sparks; in the same build as cut 1 that is one round of validation, not two. Tests that lean on a load taking 5 s have to hold it with .mock/serve-down instead (change.test.mjs:426-437). The count of 64 loads is from reading the tests.

cuts.title: across.test stall limit fixed and short, not 20 s x SLOW
cuts.what: SPARK_CONSOLE_CONNECT_MS is 20000 x SLOW here, so at SLOW=3 the never-connect test waits out two 60 s stalls: about 138 s of its 186 s. Healthy starts finish at the first 5 s look and never reach this limit, so a fixed 6000 gives the same stall, the same message and the same second try in about 30 s.
cuts.risk: Low. No assertion changes: stopped early, the words 'within N seconds', the second try over plain sockets and the put-back are all still checked. The file drops from 329 s to about 215 s (114 s of test time), which also lowers the floor when more files run at once. heal-more.test.mjs:21 sets the same value but nothing stalls there.

cuts.title: Stand-in docker without mkdir, touch and grep|cut|sed on every call
cuts.what: Every stand-in docker call first runs mkdir and touch (line 13), and docker port runs grep|cut|sed (line 179). A scan makes about 17 docker calls; operations, GPU checks and the watcher make many more. Bash tests and a read loop do the same with no extra process: about 50 fewer process starts per scan (12%).
cuts.risk: Low: stand-in only, and its output must stay the same. The saving assumes time follows process starts (not measured). Overlaps with cuts 1 and 2.

cuts.title: Run the longest files first
cuts.what: node --test sorts files by name, so validate (271 s) and workflows (304 s) start last. Give node:test's run() an ordered file list, longest first (or a small pool in lock.mjs): 1210 to 1166 s at 2 at once, 737 to 585 s at 4, 491 to 329 s at 8. It can also print each file's wall time.
cuts.risk: Low: same files, same tests, same strict mode. lock.mjs then has to pass SPARK_TEST_STRICT and pick the reporter itself, and the order needs a refresh when files change size. On the Mac more than 2 at once slows every file, so the gain at 4 to 8 at once is for Spark 2.

cuts.title: wait_operation and waitJob wake when the operation moves, not on a 1 s poll
cuts.what: wait_operation checks once a second, so each of about 130 operations is reported about half a second late; waitJob (20-desired.mjs:113), used by the one-tap validation and the gateway, polls the same way. Resolve both from step() and from the job's end instead of sleeping.
cuts.risk: Low. Neither is in a workflow fingerprint. Leave cancelJobsAndWait (20-desired.mjs:110) as it is: that one is in stop's fingerprint.

cuts.title: Downloads on the stand-in: no 4 s tail wait, shorter steps, a hold file instead of sleep 16
cuts.what: After a download ends, the job still waits out its progress watcher's sleep(4000); let that sleep end with the download. The stand-in hf takes 4 x 1 s (test/mock/bin/hf:20) and 16 s for hf-slow (hf:6), and change.test.mjs:625 sleeps 3 s: use 0.2 s steps, hold hf-slow on a file the test removes, and wait for the job's Downloading step.
cuts.risk: Line 380 is inside downloadVersion, which is in the start workflows' fingerprint, so that part belongs in the same build as cuts 1 and 3. The stand-in and test parts alone save about 14 s with no service change.

cuts.title: ask_sparkie's 40 s wait configurable on the stand-in
cuts.what: ask_sparkie waits a fixed 40 s before answering 'thinking' (also line 103); ask.test.mjs:45-57 makes the stand-in take 45 s to cross it. A wait knob honoured only with ALL_LOCAL (4 s) and an 8 s answer exercise the same path: the file drops from 101 s to about 65 s.
cuts.risk: Weakens the test slightly: today it proves the real 40 s wait works end to end with spark ask's own time limits; with a knob only the mechanism is proven. Marked so it can be dropped.

cuts.title: First cable test delay configurable; state.test waits for it instead of sleeping to 22 s
cuts.what: The service tests the cables a fixed 20 s after it starts (setTimeout ending at line 97); state.test.mjs:227 sleeps until 22 s so that test can't count as an answer from the frozen Spark. A first-test knob (1 s for that fleet) and waiting until GET /fabric shows a check newer than startedAt take about 20 s off a 62 s test.
cuts.risk: Low; not in a workflow fingerprint. The file only gets about 15 s shorter (its other chain takes 49 s), and nothing on a loaded machine, where that chain takes 101 s. Worth doing mainly because the sleep is a wall-clock assumption.

cuts.title: Watcher's first look and status interval shorter for fleet.test's fleet
cuts.what: The watcher first looks a fixed 15 s after the service starts; fleet.test's 'workloads lists the containers' waits about 10 s for it, and its /health test waits 9 s for two 5 s status looks to count spark1 offline. A first-look knob (1 s) and statusMs 1000 for this file's fleet take about 15 s off a 46 s file.
cuts.risk: Low. Set it only for fleet.test's fleet: heal.test's setup is written for a watcher that starts 15 s in. A 1 s status interval starts more processes in the background while the file runs.

cuts.title: gateway.test: the 15 s scan cache configurable instead of a 16 s sleep
cuts.what: The test sleeps 16 s to outlast recentInventory's fixed 15 s (service/src/16-actions.mjs:391). Read that 15 s from a knob honoured only with ALL_LOCAL (2 s for this file's fleet) and poll GET /v1/models until the stopped model is gone: about 13 s less waiting.
cuts.risk: Low. A shorter cache means a few more scans in this file (about 4 s each on the Mac), so the net is small there and larger on Spark 2. Keep 15 s for door and fuzz, whose reads depend on it; the heal pass reads the same cache.

flaky: test/sparkie.test.mjs:363-378 (busy 409, five at once 429, a member's 429): answers that 'take 1 seconds' sent 400, 150 and 300 ms apart have to overlap. Instead hold the stand-in model's answer on a release file, wait until model-requests.jsonl shows the held requests, assert, then release.

test/ask.test.mjs:173-179 (agents answer in slots of their own): two fixed 500 ms sleeps before expecting 'busy', and a hold of 3 x SLOW + 3 s that the later checks must fit inside. Instead wait for the held request to appear in model-requests.jsonl, and hold the answer on a release file rather than for N seconds.

test/change.test.mjs:426-437 ('already-starting' and 'already changing on Spark 3'): pass only because the start is still running, which today is the 5 s load poll plus slow scans. On a fast machine (Spark 2) the start can finish first. Instead write spark3's .mock/serve-down before the start, make the checks, then remove it.

test/change.test.mjs:625 (a stop leaves the download running): sleeps 3 s and assumes the download has begun, with the stand-in's sleep 16 as the window. Instead wait until the job's step says Downloading, and hold the stand-in hf on a file the test removes after the stop.

test/state.test.mjs:227 (two timed-out commands mark a Spark offline): sleeps until 22 s after service start, assuming the service's own cable test at 20 s is over; under load it can still be running and its answer resets the miss count. Instead wait until GET /fabric shows checkedAt later than startedAt.

test/state.test.mjs:143 (SIGTERM): sleeps 300 ms and assumes the service has taken the signal; if it has not, the next stop_model call starts a real stop. Instead poll /health until it reports that it is stopping (add that field if it is missing) before sending the call.
test/pause.test.mjs:49 (paused after three failures): sleeps 300 ms, then expects halted. Instead waitFor the settings to show halted and autoPaused.
test/gateway.test.mjs:59: a 16 s sleep to outlast a 15 s cache. Instead poll GET /v1/models until the stopped model is no longer listed.

test/internet.test.mjs:147 (signing out ends the live stream): sleeps 500 ms and assumes the /metrics stream is open. Instead wait for that request's response (status 200) before deleting the session.

test/heal.test.mjs:128: allows 3 s x SLOW for spark3's heal on the argument that it was recorded during the previous test. Instead wait for the healing event with the same 60 s limit the other heal waits use.

Every agent-door call that plans before answering (start_model, stop_model, restart_model in change, workflows, desired, gateway, pause, heal): the door answers [still_running] after a fixed 50 s (service/src/20-mcp.mjs:213) that SLOW does not stretch. With a scan at 11-20 s under load, two or three scans cross it; only across.test.mjs:32 handles that. Fewer scans (cuts 1, 2) is the fix; failing that, follow the operation through recent_operations as across does.

summary:
Fixed waits cost about 690 of the 2034 test-seconds in the quiet run (gate18.log), and about 530 of them can go without touching an assertion. At two files at once that is roughly 265 s off the 1066 s gate, to about 800 s.

Nothing was run: the counts come from reading the tests and the three logs, so treat each saving as an estimate. The firmest are the first two cuts; the stream-delay one (cut 6) is the softest.

- **Where the waits are:** about half is the literal 5 s the service sleeps before its first look at a starting model (about 50 times), and the across test sitting through a 60 s connect limit twice. The rest is downloads, the 45 s `ask_sparkie` answer, one-second operation polls and a few fixed sleeps in tests.
- **Machine speed:** the savings are in absolute seconds. An earlier, faster run (gate9.log: 569 s wall, 1047 test-seconds) carried nearly the same waits, so on Spark 2 they would be more than half the run. On the Mac the remainder is the cost of starting processes, which is outside this angle.
- **What `SPARK_TEST_SLOW=3` lengthens:** only two waits that are actually sat through: the connect limit in `test/across.test.mjs:22` and the answer holds in `test/ask.test.mjs:173`.
- **Flaky installs:** the agent door's literal 50 s answer limit (`service/src/20-mcp.mjs:213`) is not scaled for a slow machine. In gate6.log five failure lines are `start_model took over 50 seconds`.
- **Tests that must change with the cuts:** cuts 1, 3 and 5 remove time that a few tests lean on as "still loading" or "still downloading". Those tests need a hold file in the same change; each is named in the cut's risk.

No cut weakens a test. The frozen-Spark waits in `test/state.test.mjs` (20–45 s command timeouts) are left alone: scaling them down risks false timeouts on the loaded Mac.

summary:
The harness itself is not where the gate's time goes, so harness cuts are worth about 150 s of a 1066 s run (14%). Nothing was run for this: every figure comes from the gate logs and the code, and every saving is an estimate.

- **Fleet cost:** a whole fleet from start to stop takes 0.65 s on a quiet laptop and 4.2 s on a loaded one. The suite starts 27 of them. Time outside tests is 4–8% of the run.
- **Where the time goes:** on the laptop it is process starts. One library scan of the stand-in fleet is about 450 of them, and the same tests took 1047 s of file time in gate9, 2034 s in gate18 and 4750 s in gate25. gate18 was not a quiet-machine floor; gate9 ran the suite in 569 s.
- **SPARK_TEST_SLOW=3:** it lengthens three real waits, about 86 s of file time; everything else is limits. It does not reach the service's own 50 s and 20–45 s limits, which is where the loaded-laptop failures came from.
- **Concurrency:** `--test-concurrency` counts files. Tests inside a file run one after another unless a describe asks otherwise. Files share only ports and CPU, so the laptop's limit is process starts, not collisions.
- **Sharing a fleet:** door, cli and fuzz could share one (same options, read-only), saving about 7 s of file time. I would not do it. Every other file changes containers, the pause switch, memory, the desired list, the clock or the passkey, or needs its own environment.
- **Spark 2:** the gate cannot pass there today. Stand-in Sparks would read the real `/proc/meminfo`, and the real releases folder breaks two tests. Once fixed, with collision-proof ports, I estimate about 5 minutes at 4 files at once and about 3 minutes at 8–12 with SLOW=1; this is not measured.
- **Quick check:** nine light files cover 78% of the tests in 1–1.5 minutes on a quiet laptop.

I could not list running processes (permission denied), so the check for leftover fleets rests on folder timestamps: ten stale folders, none active.

cuts.what: A script beside lock.mjs that never writes the lock: build, door, passkey, internet, cli, api, agent-setup, fuzz, sparkie at concurrency 3. That is 516 of 659 tests (78%) in 77 s of file time on a quiet laptop (gate9), 181 s in gate18. A second, optional step adds the heavy files for the parts changed since the lock (17-changes: change, desired; 08-cluster: across, heal-more; 18-workflows: workflows, validate).
cuts.risk: It skips the long change, heal and two-Spark files, so it can pass where the gate fails. lock.mjs could run these nine first and stop on a failure: the same tests, but a failing gate then costs minutes instead of 18-40.

flaky: Service limits that SPARK_TEST_SLOW cannot reach: the 50 s action wait (20-mcp.mjs:213, 14-chats.mjs:101 and :306) and command timeouts of 20-45 s (e.g. 05-library.mjs:82 and :335). gate6 failed on them at validate.test.mjs:86 and :105 and workflows.test.mjs:111, :145 and :163. Fix: one scale variable honoured only under ALL_LOCAL, set from SLOW in start-mock.mjs:145; state.test.mjs:220's fleet keeps 1 because its 40 s freeze is sized to the real timeouts.

state.test.mjs:227 sleeps until 22 s after the service started so the 20 s cable test is over before the Spark freezes; a cable test slower than 2 s answers for spark2 and resets the miss count. Fix: let that fleet switch the cable test off (settable first delay at 06-links.mjs:93) and drop the sleep.

state.test.mjs:143 sleeps 300 ms after SIGTERM, then expects a new operation to be refused; a service that has not yet run its handler accepts it. Fix: /health reports `stopping` once it is draining (24-handler.mjs:54), and the test waits for that.

state.test.mjs:81-88 with :23: the state copy repeats every 60 s, so when the test is reached more than a minute after start the second copy's .part file is in the folder. gate26 failed exactly so ('no .part left behind'). Fix: SPARK_CONSOLE_BACKUP_MS=86400000 for that fleet (only the first copy is checked).

ask.test.mjs:171-187 holds two answers for a fixed time and sleeps 500 ms twice, expecting both to be still answering. Fix: a stand-in model rule that answers when a file appears; wait for /health replying = 2, assert, then release.

sparkie.test.mjs:362-378 uses 'take 1 seconds' answers with 400, 150 and 300 ms sleeps, not scaled by SLOW, to hit 409 and 429. Fix: the same hold-until-released rule, waiting on /health replying before each assertion.

heal.test.mjs:186 writes 'started 20 s ago' against a 60 s minimum run; if seeing it run and then seeing the crash takes over 40 s, it is healed instead of skipped. Fix: a stand-in docker knob that reports the start as N seconds before the inspect, or write the start time just before crash().
internet.test.mjs:147 sleeps 500 ms for the live stream to be open before deleting the session; a slower stream opens after the delete and gets 401. Fix: wait for the stream's 200 response headers.

setClock (passkey.test.mjs:129, internet.test.mjs:29, pause.test.mjs:22) writes the offset and sleeps 400 ms while clock.mjs re-reads on a 100 ms timer. Fix: clock.mjs checks the file's modification time inside Date.now(); the 11 sleeps go.
pause.test.mjs:49 sleeps 300 ms and then expects agents to be paused. Fix: waitFor the settings to show halted, then assert the rest.
change.test.mjs:625 sleeps 3 s so the download has begun before the stop. Fix: wait until the job's step or log shows the download running.
sparkie.test.mjs:87 expects two tool results in call order; gate19 got them in finish order and failed (a race, not a clock). Fix: script the two calls as two rounds so the order is fixed.

state.test.mjs:236 and :249 and door.test.mjs:301 assert 'answered at once' as an absolute 3 s or 5 s, not multiplied by SLOW. The reply text already proves the answer came from the offline memo. Scaling these with SLOW changes a threshold, so it is the owner's call.
start-mock.mjs:122 gives the service 30 s to answer /health, not multiplied by SLOW (lib.mjs:24 does not pass it). No log shows it failing, but it is the one harness limit SLOW misses.

gate22: the laptop slept mid-run (tests report about 16,000 s each, 56 failures). On macOS lock.mjs can hold the machine awake for the run with `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` and warn when on battery. Neither applies on Spark 2.
